name: NETSENSAI Shield
author: Rafal Gierlicki

sections.description:
NETSENSAI Shield offers a range of security features, including:
* Changing the login URL to minimize brute force attack risks.
* Disabling the REST API (WP API JSON) for non-logged-in users.
* Disabling XML-RPC to prevent unauthorized access.
* Disabling the WordPress file editor to avoid accidental or malicious changes.
* Disabling Application Passwords to block unauthorized API access.
* Applying critical security headers (e.g., HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) for enhanced protection.

The free version provides essential security functionalities. A PRO version with additional features is available for users seeking extended protection.
sections.installation:
1. Download NETSENSAI Shield from the WordPress.org repository or manually upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/netsensai-shield/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin from the WordPress Admin Dashboard under “Plugins”.
  3. Navigate to Settings > Secure Options and configure the plugin according to your requirements.
sections.faq:
How do I change the WordPress login URL?

Navigate to Settings > Secure Options after installing the plugin. In the “Change Login URL” field, enter your preferred custom URL (for example, change /wp-login.php to /secure_login/) and save your changes.

How does disabling the WP API JSON improve security?

Disabling the WP API JSON for users who are not logged in minimizes the exposure of your site’s data through the REST API, reducing the risk of unauthorized data access.

Why disable XML-RPC?

XML-RPC is often targeted in brute force attacks. Disabling it helps protect your site against attempts to exploit this protocol for unauthorized access.

What is the effect of disabling the file editor?

Disabling the file editor prevents direct editing of plugin and theme files through the WordPress dashboard, safeguarding against inadvertent or malicious code changes. You will need to perform any code modifications manually (e.g., via FTP).
